thread:
alex_chen: heads up — we're seeing RDMA/NVLINK retransmits and PCIe errors in eu-west-2 racks causing spikey tail latency for dedicated tenants.  p99 generation latency up ~3x for a few slices.
liam_sre: ack. can you paste the query you used?
alex_chen: ran `telemetry.query("gpu.net.errors", region=\"eu-west-2\", last=15m)` — lots of rx_crc and link_down spikes. also noticed increased egress queueing on node-*-rack3.
maria_ops: ops-bot created INC-2026 for tracking. @ops-bot can you attach the pod list for affected slices? :eyes:
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026 created. Affected resources attached: tenantA-slice-42, tenantB-dedicated-11, slice-warmpool-7.
devon_infra: this smells like NVLINK firmware flap + a recent NIC driver tweak we rolled last week. same-night rollouts touched eu-west-2 NICs.
liam_sre: +1 on firmware suspicion. nvlink counters on host look like soft resets. any thermal alarms?
alex_chen: thermal stable. NVLINK error counters and pcie post-code 43 on a subset of cards. I can repro with a synthetic RDMA burst: `bench-rdma --target node-xx --concurrency 64` shows packet drops.
sam_plat: quick mitigation idea: temporarily steer affected tenants to preemptible pooled hosts (no dedicated), and enable egress shaping on the rack to protect high-slo tenants. cost hit but keeps service. thoughts?
nina_eng: steering sounds sensible. will need a fallback policy for model-version pinning — some teams expect exact model variants. we can serve a quantized variant as fallback if pinned model not available.
maria_ops: cost tradeoff: moving two large tenants to preemptible for 3–6 hours ~ est $1.8k extra GPU-hours. ops is ok if we cap to 2 hours and then reassess.
devon_infra: implementable plan: 1) soft-quarantine noisy hosts (egress DP rules) 2) reroute new allocations away from affected racks 3) migrate active low-slo sessions off dedicated slices to preemptible warm-pool 4) schedule firmware rollback to previous NIC driver in a canary rack 5) monitor.
liam_sre: we should also add a short-term scheduler tweak: prefer same-az but different top-of-rack for tenants with high-egress. reduces cross-rack NVLINK crossing. small patch: `--prefer-tor-separation=1` in allocator.
alex_chen: I'll run the reroute now on canary tenants (tenantC small) and run an RDMA burst test.
ops-bot: Change logged: reroute policy applied to tenantC (canary).
liam_sre: canary telemetry looks good after reroute — p99 back to baseline. Alex, start migration plan for tenantA -> preemptible pool, limit window 2h.
alex_chen: starting migration, will post progress.
maria_ops: reminder: notify SRE rotation and customers of short degradation window. Draft message ready, pinging legal for wording.
devon_infra: postmortem next steps: validate driver rollback benefits, add NVLINK CRC threshold alarm, add scheduler flag for tor-separation as v2 rollout, and cost playbook for emergency preemptible spill.
liam_sre: thanks — if rollback doesn't help we'll shard affected GPUs out of dedicated pools until a permanent fix.
nina_eng: also raising a follow-up to provide model-fallback compatibility matrix so product teams can be auto-routed without surprises.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026 updated: state=mitigating, owner=devon_infra, sla-impact=partial, est-mitigation=2h."
